## Overview

Emory University is a leading research university that fosters excellence and attracts world-class talent to innovate today and prepare leaders for the future. We welcome candidates who can contribute to the excellence of our academic community.

## Job Description

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

* Supports the acquisition, management and analysis of data from multiple sites or sources.
* Supports the configuration and management of technology solutions supporting the receipt, transformation, validation and storage of data.
* Ensures that the uses of data through reports and queries are appropriate.
* Serves as an organizational consultant on matters relating to databases by providing expertise to assist users in meeting their needs.
* Develops automated quality control procedures to assess quality of data and provides reports to data owners.
* Works effectively within a group setting in areas of design of data collection instruments, database management, analysis of data, and creation of reports and dashboards.
* Develops and performs appropriate analyses.
* Provides explanations of analysis methods, assumptions made, and assists in interpretation of results and implications therein.
* Documents methods and results through development and maintenance of standard documentation artifacts including data dictionaries, standard operating procedures and analysis methodology descriptions.
* Works with onsite or field-based counterparts to coordinate consistent implementation of data quality control measures and provision of access to the central data repositories.
* Performs related responsibilities as assigned.

ADDITIONAL JOB DETAILS:

* Supports the clinical efficiency and quality improvement mission of the HOG Center for Clotting and Bleeding Disorders, Pediatric, through data analysis, reporting, and technology solutions across Emory and Children's Healthcare of Atlanta.
* Partners with clinical leadership and the Epic IT team to design and implement Smart Forms within Healthy Planet as the center's foundational population health management initiative.
* Develops and maintains Epic dashboards and reporting tools that provide real-time insight into clinical efficiency, care delivery, and patient outcomes.
* Manages and analyzes data from multiple sources across Emory and CHOA systems, ensuring accuracy, consistency, and appropriate use.
* Develops automated quality control procedures and delivers regular reports to clinical and administrative stakeholders.
* Designs data collection instruments in collaboration with clinical staff and documents all methods, workflows, and results through data dictionaries, standard operating procedures, and analysis methodology descriptions.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

* A bachelor's degree in computer science or a related field, and three years of experience in processes and standards related to data, OR an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.
* Experience with relational database management systems such as, Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL preferred.
* Experience with statistical packages such as, SAS, SPSS, R preferred.

Role Summary

The Data Analyst is an individual contributor who has moved beyond supervised execution and is developing the independence, analytical depth, and stakeholder skills needed to progress to Senior level. They own smaller analytical domains end-to-end, contribute meaningfully to team standards, and begin to proactively surface insights rather than waiting to be directed.

What You'll Do

Analytics & Insight Delivery

- Deliver analytical work end-to-end for assigned business areas — from scoping and analysis through to presentation and stakeholder follow-through — with minimal re-direction

- Support ad-hoc analysis for internal stakeholders including Marketing, Product, Finance, and Account Management, providing interpretive framing alongside data outputs rather than data retrieval alone

- Begin to proactively surface trends, anomalies, and data-driven observations to stakeholders, developing the instinct to flag what matters without being asked

- Support A/B test experiments under the guidance of the Senior DA — including data preparation, metric tracking, and results summaries — building toward independent experimental design at Senior level

Google Analytics & Data Collection

- Support the Senior DA in GA4 reporting, tracking plan validation, and custom dimension and metric implementation

- Develop working knowledge of GA-to-warehouse integration and tagging practices in preparation for owning this domain at Senior level

BI Development & Semantic Layer

- Design, build, and maintain Looker dashboards and Explores for assigned business areas, owning deliverables with limited rework

- Develop LookML including dimensions, measures, derived tables, and Explore configurations — ensuring all work is documented and consistent with team standards

- Contribute to the shared semantic layer by flagging metric definition inconsistencies and proposing resolutions in collaboration with the Senior DA and Analytics Engineering team

- Expand self-service analytics for non-technical stakeholders, enabling them to answer their own questions and reducing ad-hoc request volume to the team

- Maintain accuracy and consistency of production Explores and dashboards as underlying data warehouse structures evolve

Company Description

We’re Checkout.com. You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day.

We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers.

Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale.

If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact.

With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started.

About the team Payment Success Management (PSM) is a merchant-facing team that diagnoses and fixes payment performance problems. When a merchant's approval rate falls short of expectations or trails another payment provider, we find out why and close the gap. This role supports US-based merchants and works with our account managers and technical account managers.

The kind of problems you'll solve

- A merchant's approval rate dropped 3 points last month, and nobody knows why.

- One issuing bank is declining far more of a merchant's cards than its peers.

- Our machine-learning optimization engine keeps making the wrong routing or retry decision for a specific bank or card type.

- A merchant is comparing us with another provider that calculates success differently, and we need to agree on what "good" looks like.

Merchants tell us there's a problem, not where it is. You'll find it, test a fix and prove the result.

How you'll make an impact

- Run merchant engagements from start to finish, usually about three months each.

- Investigate large, complex payment datasets in SQL and Python to find the root cause of performance gaps.

- Turn findings into hypotheses, design A/B tests and other experiments, and measure the uplift.

- Learn how our ML optimization engine makes decisions, spot where it gets things wrong, and work with our ML engineers to fix it. You won't build the models; you'll work out why they decide what they do.

- Explain your findings to merchants and non-technical colleagues clearly and persuasively.

- Use automation and AI to make the team's daily work more efficient, and share what you learn across teams.

What we're looking for

- 5+ years of full-time experience using data to diagnose and improve a business metric, such as approval rate, conversion, revenue, cost or retention. We're looking for metrics you changed, not reports you delivered.

- Hands-on experience designing or analyzing experiments: A/B tests, holdouts or controlled comparisons.

- Strong SQL and Python for analysis. You can check your own queries, and AI-generated code, for accuracy. You don't need to write production code, and we'll teach you Go.

- Curiosity about problems without a ready-made answer.

- The ability to explain complex analysis simply to non-technical audiences.

Payments experience isn't required; you'll learn it in your first weeks. We'd especially like to hear from people with consulting backgrounds, where you linked client teams and technical teams, or startup backgrounds, where you owned and optimized something end to end.

This role probably isn't for you if…

- Most of your recent work is building dashboards and reports for other teams to act on.

- Your focus is data engineering, building pipelines and data infrastructure.

- Your focus is building, training and deploying ML models.

These are valuable skills and you'll use some of them here, but this role is mainly investigation and experimentation.

Logistics

- Hybrid: Tuesday–Thursday in our Midtown Atlanta office (Colony Square).

- This role does not offer relocation assistance or visa sponsorship.

Additional Information

Bring all of you to work

We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one.

Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands.

We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here.

It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable.

Life at Checkout.com http://Checkout.com

We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection.

Curious about what it’s like to be part of our team? Visit our Careers Page https://www.checkout.com/careers to learn more about our culture, open roles, and what drives us.

For a closer look at daily life at Checkout.com http://Checkout.com, follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/checkout/life/ and Instagram https://www.instagram.com/checkout_com/

**About Us**

DLH delivers improved health and national security readiness solutions for federal programs through science research and development, systems engineering and integration, and digital transformation. Our experts in public health, performance evaluation, and health operations solve the complex problems faced by civilian and military customers alike by leveraging advanced tools – including digital transformation, artificial intelligence, data analytics, cloud enablement, modeling, and simulation, and more. DLH is dedicated to the idea that “Your Mission is Our Passion” and brings a unique combination of government sector experience, proven methodology, and unwavering commitment to innovation to improve the lives of millions.

**Overview**

DLH Corp. is looking for a Public Health **Data Analyst** using **R and** SAS to join our talented and innovative team supporting the **Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)**. This is a hybrid work environment based out of Atlanta, GA. Teleworking most days, with visits to the CDC campus for in-person meetings and ad hoc office visits.

CDC’s National Center for HIV/AIDS, Viral Hepatitis, STD, and TB Prevention (NCHHSTP), the Division of HIV Prevention (DHP) is charged with preventing HIV infection and reducing the incidence of HIV-related illness and death. The overarching objectives of the contract held by DLH are to assist DHP in addressing its public health mission by providing data management, data governance, data analysis, and data dissemination support to strengthen the nationwide capacity to monitor the HIV epidemic. As such, DLH is seeking an Atlanta-based **Data Analyst** with the following skills:

**Responsibilities**

* Provide analytic support (R and SAS) for established analyses of National HIV surveillance data, including descriptive analyses, frequency tables, data quality review, and production and dissemination of standardized surveillance products to support HIV prevention and care planning, program monitoring, resource allocation, and public health decision-making.
* Provide statistical support (R and SAS) for complex analyses of National HIV surveillance data, including incidence and lifetime risk estimation, statistical modeling, regression and trend analyses, and surveillance variable development and validation, to support scientifically rigorous national HIV surveillance products used for public health planning, resource allocation, and decision-making.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in public health, statistics, or related field.
* 2 years of strong demonstrated experience working with existing and developing new R and SAS scripts.
* Demonstrated ability to work with multiple data sources to monitor and assess data to ensure data quality, including accuracy and completeness.
* Strong critical thinking and communication skills.
* Eagerness to learn and apply skills to challenging projects.
* Clear communication (written and verbal).
* Must be able to obtain a Public Trust clearance
    

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master’s degree in public health, statistics, or related field.
* Experience working with surveillance data.
* Knowledge of HIV data and public health surveillance systems.
* Experience with large (>500,000 observations), document-based datasets.
* Detail-oriented and able to create meticulous documentation of variables, datasets, and data attributes with a commitment to generating accurate data and products.
* Strong organizational and interpersonal skills.

**Basic Compensation: $60,000 - $65,000 yearly salary**

The salary range listed reflects what we reasonably expect to pay for this role at the time of posting. The final offer may vary based on skills, experience, geographic location, market conditions, and internal equity. Additional compensation may include performance incentives and program-specific awards. We do not use salary history to determine compensation, in line with applicable law.

**Benefits**

DLH Corp offers our employees an excellent benefits package, including Personal Time Off (PTO), medical, dental, vision, supplemental life with AD&D, disability coverage, flexible spending accounts, and more. We want our employees to save for their future; therefore, we offer a 401(k) Retirement Plan, which includes a matching component. DLH is dedicated to your career development, providing training to help drive success, with access to our best-in-class e-learning suite for formal and informal learning, professional and technical certification preparation, and education assistance at accredited institutions.

**EEO**

DLH Corporation is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment.  DLH will provide reasonable accommodation to individuals with disabilities and disabled Veterans who need assistance to apply.

DLH is committed to maintaining a fair and authentic interview process
